scope: Domain F (public procurement) + Domain G (hiring): 10 source_ids
connector_notes: eu_ted is VERIFIED_API but deliberately has NO connector: its search index returns winner-name/winner-partname as null, so an award record built from it would have no supplier. Emitting supplier-less awards would be worse than emitting none.
china_ccgp is VERIFIED_PUBLIC_QUERY but has NO connector: HTML-only, mixed notice/award listing, captcha field on the form, no supplier identifier in the listing.
sam_gov / workday_phenom / company_careers_pages / ocds_registry have no connector by design (registration-gated, per-tenant, client-rendered, standards-layer).

real_records_collected.note: records actually returned by live requests during probing; connectors were additionally live-smoked (see connector_smoke)

connector_smoke.method: live run of all four connectors through base.HttpClient, one bounded page each

deliverables.samples_note: workday_phenom has no SAMPLES.json because every request failed (TLS hostname mismatch / 404) — no response body exists to store

blocked.reason: api_key is documented as mandatory; no account was created and no key used. Gateway answers unauthenticated requests with 404 (empty body), not 401/403, so the registration requirement is a documented fact plus an observed refusal.
No vendor-neutral API. jobs.medtronic.com resolves but its TLS certificate does not match the hostname (verification deliberately not disabled); Workday CXS tenant/site guesses returned 404.

HTML front doors only: 2 of 4 firm pages returned 200, 1 returned 403, 1 returned 404, and the one job-listing page is client-rendered so the served HTML contains no vacancies. No publication timestamp.

ted.europa.eu answers this client with a JavaScript 'Human Verification' challenge on both the notice XML link and the bulk-downloads page. Not bypassed, so anonymous bulk XML is UNVERIFIED; the search API itself is verified.
Not a blocker but a category limit: OCDS is a standard plus a publisher registry, not a record publisher, so it cannot be 'verified' as a data source.

five_firm_identifiability.question: Can Medtronic / GE HealthCare / Philips / Dräger / Mindray be identified in real procurement and hiring records?
five_firm_identifiability.procurement_identifiable: YES for all five on USAspending, with caveats

detail.Medtronic: 10/10 first-page recipient names resolve exact_alias (MEDTRONIC CARE MANAGEMENT SERVICES, LLC et al.); token-search population 97,663 contract actions (upper bound, not a firm count); page amounts 27.0M-69.2M USD; performance starts 2013-2024.
detail.GE HealthCare: only 1/10 first-page names resolve (GE MEDICAL SYSTEMS INFORMATION TECHNOLOGIES); 9/10 are CHANGE HEALTHCARE entities caught by the 'HealthCare' token. Population 5,692 is therefore polluted; a cleaner query must use 'GE MEDICAL SYSTEMS' or 'GE HEALTHCARE'.
detail.Philips: 10/10 resolve (PHILIPS NORTH AMERICA LLC, PHILIPS MEDICAL SYSTEMS NORTH AMERICA, PHILIPS RS NORTH AMERICA); population 33,929; page amounts 24.4M-232.7M USD; starts 2006-2021.
detail.Draeger: 10/10 resolve (DRAEGER INC); population 22,725; page amounts 3.04M-31.2M USD; starts 2013-2026.
detail.Mindray: 10/10 resolve (MINDRAY DS USA INC); population only 43 contract actions; page amounts 53.5K-200.9K USD; starts 2011-2019 — very small US federal footprint.

five_firm_identifiability.hiring_detail: None of the five has a public Greenhouse or Lever board under its likely token, while the control tokens (stripe: 766 jobs; leverdemo: 10 postings) resolved in the same runs. Their hiring data sits behind per-employer Phenom/Workday-style stacks.
five_firm_identifiability.important_caveat: USAspending is a token search, not an entity-resolution service: population counts are upper bounds and must be recomputed after identity resolution. An award is an obligation, not revenue.

procurement_chain_layering.notice_to_revenue: notice → award → contract signed → delivery → realised revenue

what_is_observable.notice: uk_find_a_tender (tag 'tender') and eu_ted (notice-type cn-standard); NOT available from usaspending
what_is_observable.award: uk_find_a_tender (tag 'award', supplier named + OCDS org id), usaspending (award action, recipient named, obligation amount); eu_ted search index does NOT expose the winner
what_is_observable.contract_signed: uk_find_a_tender contracts[0].dateSigned only; usaspending has date_signed on the detail endpoint
what_is_observable.delivery: not observable in any source probed
what_is_observable.revenue: not observable in any source probed — federal obligations are not revenue

procurement_chain_layering.explicitly_forbidden_mapping: An announcement is not an award (TED full-text hits are keyword mentions, not awards), an award is not a signed contract (USAspending has no contract-signature semantics for all rows), and neither is revenue.

time_semantics_findings: USAspending publishes NO publication clock: event dates only. source_public_at is left empty with quality 'unknown' in the connector rather than borrowing 'Start Date' (period-of-performance start).

UK FTS gives all four clocks distinctly: source_public_at = release.date, event_at = contracts[0].dateSigned, first_observed_at = fetch clock. awards[0].date was null in every probed record, so it is not used.
TED publishes publication-date (with offset) but no winner; its notice publication date is a genuine publication clock for the notice stage only.
Greenhouse first_published is a true publication clock; updated_at is an edit time and is stored separately (never as source_public_at).
Lever createdAt is epoch MILLISECONDS with no updatedAt; converted once, in one place, so an edit cannot masquerade as a new posting.
China CCGP announcement timestamps have day+time precision but the listing mixes notice/award/failure/correction, so the timestamp's meaning depends on the announcement type.
product_identity_findings: No procurement source probed carries a device identifier. USAspending has a free-text Description (<=134 chars observed); TED has CPV categories (33100000 = medical equipments) but no model; UK FTS has CPV + tender items with delivery regions only.
Therefore: contract → specific device linking is NOT possible from structured fields in any probed source. Only keyword hits in free text are possible, with unknown precision/recall.
CPV 33100000 matched 488,133 TED notices — that is a category, not a product: it cannot be joined to UDI/510(k) and must not be presented as product-level evidence.

Recommendation for the study: treat procurement as firm-level demand evidence at best; a model-level procurement claim would need a different source class (e.g. award line items or hospital purchase orders), which was not found here.
hiring_discipline_findings: Hiring volume is not a technology signal. Every connector carries an explicit interpretation_warning in normalized and in the register's known_limitations.

Role split: Greenhouse exposes NO department/function field (metadata null on all 766 probed postings), so an R&D/Sales/Production split there is a title-text heuristic only. Lever exposes categories.department, but it was null for some postings, so coverage must be measured (department_coverage()).
Publication clock vs observation clock: first_published (Greenhouse) / createdAt (Lever) is source_public_at; first_observed_at equals the fetch clock and is never back-filled.

Re-posting duplication: the required (company, title, location) key is implemented in both connectors (duplicate_report()), which reports duplicate instances and rate instead of silently collapsing them. Observed 0 duplicates in the 3-posting smoke sample (too small to be a population statement).
overlap_with_existing_hiring_research: Possible overlap with the hiring-capability study on branch research/s031-hiring-capability-study (PR #22): that asset was not present in this worktree and was not read or modified. If it already defines role-taxonomy or posting-dedupe rules, this subpackage's duplicate_report()/department_coverage() should be reconciled with it by the Lead rather than duplicated.
notable_findings: USAspending's award search is POST-only and needs no API key; it returns real awards, but it publishes no publication date at all — so a 'when could we have known' study cannot use it alone.

USAspending recipient_search_text is a token search: 'GE HealthCare' returned CHANGE HEALTHCARE entities, and only 1 of 10 first-page names resolved to GE HealthCare. Population counts like 97,663 (Medtronic) are upper bounds, not firm award counts.

EU TED's Search API v3 answers anonymous POST queries, and notice-type cleanly separates cn-standard (contract notices, 2.95M) from can-standard (award notices, 2.86M) — but the winning supplier is NOT in the index (winner fields null even for 2024 medical awards), so TED cannot support award→supplier linkage on its own.

UK Find a Tender is the only probed source that publishes notice, award AND contract signature as distinct, dated, stage-tagged objects with a named supplier plus an OCDS organisation id. It is the best procurement source of this batch.

ted.europa.eu (web host, notice XML, bulk downloads) answers with a JavaScript 'Human Verification' challenge; that was not bypassed, so anonymous TED bulk XML is unverified and 'bulk_download_available' is UNKNOWN rather than YES.

China CCGP's keyword search answers anonymously with real dated announcements (90 for 内窥镜), which contradicts the P3 'known-blocked' assumption — but the listing mixes 采购公告/中标公告/废标公告, so it cannot be treated as a notice feed.

NEGATIVE RESULT: none of the five target firms publishes a Greenhouse or Lever job board, while control tokens resolved in the same runs (766 jobs / 10 postings). This is a fact about those two platforms, not about hiring data in general.
jobs.medtronic.com resolves but its TLS certificate does not match the hostname; the correct response was to stop, not to disable verification.
philips.wd3 and gehc.wd5 Workday CXS guesses both 404'd: tenant+site names must be discovered per employer, so a Workday adapter is per-employer work, not a generalisable connector.
open_questions: Which of the five firms' hire data is reachable at all without JS execution? A real answer needs per-employer discovery (Workday tenant/site, Phenom board id), which is out of scope for a 20-request probe.
Is there any procurement source with award line items that name a model/part number? None of the 10 probed sources has one; that is the gap for product-level procurement evidence.

schema.canonical_key's priority list has no 'ocid' scheme, so two OCDS publishers republishing the same procurement will not de-duplicate across sources. Adding 'ocid' would require editing a frozen foundation module — flagged for the Lead, not changed here.
USAspending's bulk award archive (download centre) was not probed; if it is anonymous, it would allow population-level five-firm counts instead of token-search upper bounds.
Does the UK FTS feed allow a stable full-history walk (updatedFrom/updatedTo over years) within rate limits? Only a 7-day window was exercised.

tests.network: none - all fixtures are inline dicts; no sample file is read

notes_for_lead: All 10 register records are written with connection_status NOT_TESTED by contract; the merge tool derives the real status (verified above: 5 VERIFIED_API, 1 VERIFIED_PUBLIC_QUERY, 1 REQUIRES_REGISTRATION, 2 UNAVAILABLE, 1 NOT_TESTED) and reports 0 validation problems for these 10.

eu_ted is deliberately connector-less; if the Lead wants an EU award connector, the missing piece is the notice XML, which needs either a TED API key or a challenge-clearing client — both out of policy here.
China CCGP is a positive verification that contradicts the P3 assumption; it is documented as exploratory (mixed announcement types, no supplier ids), not as a usable panel.
